title: The group law on an elliptic curve
hook: A line through P and Q meets the cubic once more. Reflect that point and you have P + Q.
alt: A cubic curve with a line through two points P and Q that crosses it a third time; a dashed vertical line joins that crossing to its mirror image, the sum P + Q, while P slides along the curve. Engaged, either point can be dragged along the curve and the sum follows.
author: @kmoreau.geom

pointer.hint: Drag P or Q along the curve

presets.label: Split the curve: b = 0.30
presets.note: Below 2/(3√3) ≈ 0.385 the real curve has two components. The unbounded one is the identity component, and a subgroup.

presets.label: P on the oval
presets.note: With P on the oval and Q on the unbounded branch, P + Q lands back on the oval: the oval is a coset of the identity component.

presets.label: Let P slide again
presets.note: P follows its animation again and Q goes back to its place.
